SMTO-DB-0012 — The database search didn't say what kind of database it is

GUID: b95a49bc-dad9-4af3-b0f1-e79935d62a47
Slug: database-discovery-engine-required
Domain: DB · Subsystem: db

What happened

  • SMTO was asked to find the databases on a server, but the request didn't say what kind of database server it is. SMTO didn't connect to anything.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Find the request that asked SMTO to search for databases (usually sent by a script or tool someone set up), and set its engine (database type) to postgres. SMTO needs to know the database type before it can connect, and it only searches PostgreSQL servers.
  2. If the server isn't PostgreSQL, stop here and ask the person who manages SMTO how that database should be added. This search can only find PostgreSQL databases, so other types need a different setup.
  3. Send the corrected request again. Nothing was attempted the first time, so it's safe to send it again once the type is filled in.

What success looks like

  • The search lists the databases found on the server as drafts you can review.

If it still fails

  • Send the request you used, with the password removed, to the person who manages SMTO, and say what kind of database server it is. Don't put the password in that message.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A database discovery request (/api/agent/databases/discover) had an empty engine and was rejected as missing_engine before any connection was attempted.

What this means

  • Discovery normalizes the requested engine to an empty string and returns missing_engine before connection setup. Input rejection is pre-dispatch only where the producer says so. Discovery and psql failures require their original execution evidence; diagnostics do not run SQL or prove that a mutation rolled back.

Why this can happen

  • Discovery normalizes the requested engine to an empty string and returns missing_engine before connection setup.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the request engine rather than network or login state.

How to fix it

  • Set engine to postgres (or postgresql) in the DatabaseDiscoveryRequest sent to POST /api/agent/databases/discover, alongside host, port, user and password. Discovery v1 supports PostgreSQL only.
  • Select the supported postgres engine for database discovery.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported engine is explicitly selected and request validation advances.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Input rejection is pre-dispatch only where the producer says so. Discovery and psql failures require their original execution evidence; diagnostics do not run SQL or prove that a mutation rolled back.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
